Reddit just watched its stock crater almost 30% in a single session, even though Q3 2026 delivered one of its strongest reports yet. Revenue hit US$894.96 million and net income reached US$283.26 million, both solid figures for a social platform still early in its public life.

Coming into the release, the share price had already slipped over the past quarter. Today the move turned into a full sentiment reset. The question hanging over the tape is whether this selloff reflects a genuine reassessment of future risk or a market crowd reacting first and reading the earnings later.

Reddit's Bull Story Meets Hard User Metrics

Optimistic Reddit forecasts lean heavily on international traction and deeper engagement turning the platform into a global growth engine.

"Strong international expansion, AI-driven search, and deep community engagement position Reddit for outsized growth in users, advertising revenue, and strategic market share globally."

Q3 shows part of that picture coming through. International advertising revenue grew faster than the US and ARPU rose 36% to US$6.87, which points to healthier monetization per user. Reddit also added roughly 1b new posts and comments, expanding the content base. At the same time, DAUs grew 12% to 130.3m and management now guides to a low double digit DAU decline in Q4, which directly challenges the idea of uninterrupted user expansion.

title: 5 Best High Growth Stocks Outside Big Tech

The market's growth leadership has become abnormally concentrated in a small number of mega-cap technology stocks, leaving investors with fewer obvious opportunities to find rapid earnings growth outside of the AI trade. Ten AI-related stocks currently account for over 40% of the S&P 500's market capitalization, with NVDA, AAPL, and MSFT accounting for approximately 21.7% of the index. That concentration has made non-tech growth stocks more appealing, but also more selective: a company can generate strong revenue growth while struggling to justify its valuation if margins, debt, customer concentration, or capital intensity are all trending in the wrong direction. The opportunity comes from identifying businesses with long-term growth that can support multiples rather than merely riding the broader AI story, something we previously covered in our 10 High Growth Stocks Outside Tech Analysts Are Bullish On article.

The case for looking beyond mega-cap technology is that large tech companies haven't stopped growing. Their valuations already account for much of the predicted AI-driven earnings acceleration, while a number of healthcare, industrial, consumer, finance, and energy companies are growing at rates that may surprise investors.

According to Russell Investments, analysts anticipate the "Magnificent Seven" to increase third-quarter earnings by 20.3% year over year, while the other 493 companies in the S&P 500 are expected to grow by 27.7%. In other words, earnings momentum is broadening beyond the largest tech firms, potentially offering up opportunities for companies outside the AI trade.

The idea is to avoid using "growth" as a single metric. A company that grows revenue at 30% per year could still be a bad investment if it burns cash, relies on a small number of customers, or funds expansion through repeated dilution. Netskope is a good example: the cybersecurity company announced second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $220.5 million, up 29.2% year-over-year, but trailing EBITDA remained negative at $721 million, and the stock traded at about 9x sales. That is, investors are paying a premium for ongoing top-line momentum as they wait for more proof that growth can translate into durable profits. In contrast, a company growing earnings in the high teens or low twenties can be appealing if it has pricing power, recurring revenue, a strong balance sheet, and a clear path to margin improvement.

The issue is that some companies have already been rerated as "AI adjacent," even though their underlying earnings haven't yet justified the premium. That's why the best opportunities are typically identified where growth is still undervalued, rather than where the AI label has already done the majority of the work.

Key Takeaways

AppLovin stock fell 12% in the past week to a new 52-week low, mostly on Friday after weak reports from Reddit and Roblox.

Roblox's user decline is a poor guide to AppLovin, whose revenue rose 56% in the first six months of 2026 even as installs through its ads fell 10%.

Citi still rates AppLovin a Buy with a $500 target, and the Nov. 4 third-quarter report is the next test of that call.

AppLovin (APP:NASDAQ) stock is down 12% in the past week, to a new 52-week low, with no news from the company itself.

Most of it came on Friday, when the stock fell 10% to $228.50 after Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) and Roblox (RBLX:NYSE) reported weaker user numbers on Thursday evening.

Investors Sold AppLovin With Reddit and Roblox

Reddit fell 29% on Friday, its worst day since going public in 2024. Its fourth-quarter revenue forecast of $1 billion to $1.03 billion missed the $1.05 billion Wall Street expected. CEO Steve Huffman also warned that daily visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage this quarter if traffic from search engines keeps shrinking. AppLovin's ads run inside apps that don't need Google for traffic.

Roblox is off 19% for the week after its daily active users fell 9% from a year earlier, to 138 million. Gaming still makes up most of AppLovin's revenue, so Roblox's numbers matter more here. But in the first half of 2026, installs through AppLovin's ads fell 10% while net revenue per install rose 75%, its second-quarter 10-Q shows. So I'd call Friday guilt by association.

Citi Still Sees AppLovin at $500

UBS cut its target to $414 from $790 on Oct. 28, citing slower growth from consumer advertisers, and RBC cut its to $500 from $575. Citi's Jason Bazinet had already cut his target to $500 from $600 earlier in October, and he still rates the stock a Buy.

Earnings estimates have held up better. Analysts still expect normalized EPS to more than double from 2025 to 2028:

AppLovin traded at 14x forward earnings at Thursday's close, near the bottom of its five-year range, and Friday's drop took it lower still:

Citi's $500 works out to about 27x the earnings analysts expect over the next year, a bit above the stock's 25x five-year average.

AppLovin reports third-quarter results on Nov. 4. Its own guide calls for revenue of $2.06 billion to $2.09 billion, up 46% to 48% from a year earlier. On the August call, CEO Adam Foroughi put the second quarter's slight revenue miss down to timing: the next step-up in model performance "landed just after quarter end," and he said the third quarter had started strong because of it.

title: Why Reddit (RDDT) stock is trading lower today

Why Reddit (RDDT) stock is trading lower today

RDDT
Trade Reddit on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
What happened?

Shares of online community and discussion platform Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) fell 25.2% in the morning session after the company reported third-quarter 2026 financial results and issued fourth-quarter guidance that fell below Wall Street's estimates.

According to a company press release, Reddit reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $895 million, up 53% year on year, and diluted earnings per share of $1.40. Both figures exceeded Wall Street expectations, topping consensus analyst estimates of $877.2 million in revenue and $1.33 in earnings per share. However, forward-looking guidance dampened investor sentiment. Reddit projected fourth-quarter 2026 revenue between $1 billion and $1.03 billion and adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization) between $480 million and $510 million. At the midpoints of $1.02 billion and $495 million, respectively, both revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance missed consensus estimates of $1.04 billion and $509.4 million. In addition, domestic daily active visitors fell by 900,000 year on year to 50.7 million, raising concerns over domestic user traction.

On the earnings call, CEO Steve Huffman attributed user softness to search referral traffic dropping by over 1 million weekly visits in October as Google expands AI Overviews, warning that fourth-quarter daily active uniques could drop by a low-double-digit percentage. Huffman noted that logged-in and mobile app users generate over 80% of monetization, prompting tests to shift toward a logged-in-only platform.

The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks. Is now the time to buy Reddit? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

What is the market telling us

Reddit's shares are extremely volatile and have had 57 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Reddit and indicate this news significantly impacted the market's perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 18 days ago when the stock dropped 3.6% on the news that rising benchmark Treasury yields and profit-taking across communication services pressured high-valuation growth equities ahead of key inflation data.

The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield climbed four basis points to 5.27%, lifting discount rates across long-duration equities. Communication services lagged the broader market with a 1.5% morning drop, as Reddit slid toward an intraday low of $151.42 after opening near $160.90.The decline halted a multi-day advance after Needham analyst Laura Martin reaffirmed a Buy rating and a $300 price target in research carried by Tipranks.

title: Reddit stock plunges 29.2% as Google AI cuts US traffic
detail:
Reddit stock plunges 29.2% as Google AI cuts US traffic
Todd Campbell
Sat, October 31, 2026 at 9:07 AM CDT 4 min read
RDDT
GOOG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Updated to reflect Reddit closing stock price on 10/30/2026

Reddit's stock plunged 29.2% on Friday, October 30, after the company said its U.S. audience is shrinking due to Google's AI search features.

The sell-off came even though third-quarter revenue jumped 53% to $895 million. U.S. daily users fell to 50.7 million, down 2.5 million from the prior quarter, and CEO Steve Huffman said search referrals dropped by more than 1 million a week in October.

Shares, which closed at $129.60 on October 29, traded below their 52-week low of $119.27, changing hands at $91.73 at 4 pm EDT. For investors who bought Reddit as an AI winner, the message is that the same technology is now taking away the traffic that feeds the business.

Reddit is tied deeply to Google

Reddit runs the discussion forums where users post questions, advice and opinions, and it makes money mainly from advertising.

Much of its audience arrives from Google searches, which is why search changes matter so much. The stock has been popular with retail investors, but its data is also valuable to AI companies.

In 2024, Reddit inked deals with Google and OpenAI, allowing their respective Gemini and ChatGPT large language models to train on Reddit content in exchange for $60 million and $70 million per year, respectively.

Related: Googling for Reddit answers is about to get harder

Deals like that have supported revenue, but concern is that AI overviews are reducing traffic to Reddit by more than the company is pocketing from its AI deals.

Reddit reports "daily active uniques," or DAUq, split between logged-in users, who tend to be more engaged, and logged-out users, who often arrive from search and see fewer ads and less engagement. That split is the heart of today's drop.

In Q3, global DAUq rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million. However, U.S. DAUq fell 1% year-over-year, as a 4% dip in logged-out users overwhelmed a 1% increase in logged-in users.

"Google has really shifted in their relationship with the rest of the Internet," said CEO Steve Huffman on Reddit's earnings call. "People still want Reddit. It's just Google is not sending them to Reddit the way they used to."

Reddit CEO Steve Huffman saw a drop in logged-out user engagement as Google referrals fell due to AI overviews.Bloomberg / Getty Images
Reddit quarter was far from a disaster, but worries remain

Reddit revenue in the third quarter rose a more than healthy 53% to $895 million and while DAUq saw headwinds, U.S. revenue was still up 50% to $719 million.

As a result, Reddit's profit improved, with diluted EPS clocking in at $1.40, above Wall Street estimates of $1.33.

Google's AI Shift Threatens Reddit's Growth Engine

Reddit saw its U.S. daily active unique users decline by about 5% in Q3 compared to Q2, while management warned of a lower-double-digit percentage decline in the fourth.

Google search referrals are falling by more than 1 million per week, according to Citizens' data, threatening the flow of visitors who could eventually become regular, logged-in users. Analyst Andrew Boone also told clients that Google continues to crawl the platform rather heavily, but its AI Overviews and AI mode are sending fewer people back to the site.

The financial implications could emerge gradually. Advertising revenue still came in up 54% year-over-year at $847 million, demonstrating strong monetization. Sustaining that momentum, however, may become more challenging if audience losses persist and Reddit must spend more to attract replacement users.

Citizens Sees Reddit Stock as Fairly Valued

In his research note, Boone said the uncertainty surrounding user growth leaves the Reddit shares fairly valued.

In Q3, the firm's U.S. logged-out daily active uniques came in down 4% compared to last year — their first annual decline since 2022.

Citizens' concern is that weaker traffic increases pressure to extract more revenue from existing users. Higher acquisition spending in 2027 could weigh on profitability, while traffic damage could complicate data-licensing renewals.

Logged-in and app users already account for more than 80% of monetization. Any potential hit on that front, therefore, stands to weigh on RDDT's business and its share price over time.

Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) plans to move to a mostly logged-in experience, limiting casual browsing for anonymous visitors.

The shift is aimed at deepening engagement, refining ad targeting and curbing AI scraping of Reddit discussion data.

The change has drawn investor pushback and regulatory attention over whether the risks were clearly flagged to shareholders.

Reddit runs a global discussion platform within the Interactive Media and Services industry, where logged-in communities, moderators and advertisers all rely on user accounts and identity signals to function. That setup makes any shift in sign in requirements especially important for how the business connects its US$24.9b social forum ecosystem with its ad partners.

How does a logged-in Reddit experience affect the business model?

A mostly signed-in user base gives Reddit cleaner identity signals, which helps the platform sell more targeted ads and support its AI tools. The trade off is that restricting anonymous browsing can trim casual traffic, so the ad engine leans harder on depth of engagement rather than headline user counts.

Does this change the Reddit Narrative around AI data licensing?

The move lines up with the Narrative view that Reddit's conversation data is valuable for AI and licensing deals, but also highlights a key risk. Tighter access strengthens Reddit's bargaining position on renewals, while uncertainty over long term AI data contracts and reliance on digital advertising stay firmly in focus.

Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) reported third-quarter revenue growth of 53% year over year to $895 million, as advertising revenue rose 54% to $847 million. The company also said trailing 12-month revenue surpassed $3 billion, while profitability and cash generation continued to expand.

However, executives said changes in internet search are reducing referral traffic to Reddit, particularly among logged-out web users. Chief Executive Officer Steve Huffman said the decline accelerated late in the third quarter and has continued into October, prompting the company to focus more heavily on logged-in and app-based users.

Search Traffic Declines, but App and Logged-In Users Grow

Reddit's U.S. User Decline Raises a Bigger Question After Its Earnings Beat

Huffman said search-referral traffic was down "meaningfully" during the third quarter, with the largest effect on logged-out and web traffic. During October, Reddit saw search traffic fall by more than 1 million referrals per week on average, Huffman said. If that pace persists, he said current trends indicate total daily active uniques, or DAUq, could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter from the company's current base of 130 million DAUq.
